findings.title: MarketFactory.updateExtension() Missing onlyOwner Modifier Enables Total Protocol Compromise
findings.description: The updateExtension() function in MarketFactory.sol has no access control modifier, allowing any address to register itself as a protocol-wide extension. Extensions receive operator-equivalent privileges over ALL accounts in ALL markets, enabling complete fund drainage in a single transaction.

findings.title: Attack Chain: Extension Exploit + Margin Manipulation + DoS = Total Drain
findings.description: Multi-step attack combining VULN-001 (extension registration), VULN-090 (zero margin manipulation), and VULN-036 (pending order DoS) to achieve total protocol drainage. Attacker registers as extension, manipulates margins, blocks user collateral deposits, then drains all positions.

findings.title: Attack Chain: Extension + Coordinator Fee Siphon
findings.description: Combining VULN-001 extension exploit with coordinator fee mechanisms to siphon protocol revenue. Attacker registers as extension, gains operator privileges, and redirects fee accumulation to controlled addresses across all markets simultaneously.

findings.title: VerifierBase Signer-Account Mismatch Enables Systematic Nonce/Group Griefing
findings.description: cancelGroupWithSignature() and cancelNonceWithSignature() verify signatures against common.signer but operate on nonces tracked per common.account. No authorization bridge exists, allowing any address to cancel groups and consume nonces for any other account, invalidating batches of signed intent orders at minimal cost (~$1-2 on Arbitrum).

findings.title: Pending Order Limit Griefing Blocks All Collateral Deposits
findings.description: The global pending order limit (maxPendingGlobal) is shared across all accounts. An attacker placing minimum-size orders fills all slots, blocking ALL users from placing orders. Even pure collateral deposits are blocked despite being exempt from other checks. Non-recoverable attack cost ~$0.84/cycle, sustained DoS ~$63/hour on Arbitrum.

findings.title: Pending Order DoS Combined with Liquidation Protection Blocks Collateral Rescue
findings.description: When a liquidation creates a pending protected order, MarketProtectedError blocks ALL non-liquidation operations including collateral deposits. Combined with pending order DoS, users cannot add collateral to save positions during liquidation, creating a synergistic attack amplifying both vulnerabilities.

findings.title: Rebalance Config Accepts Arbitrary Addresses as Markets Enabling Fund Drainage
findings.description: Controller._updateRebalanceGroup never validates that market addresses are registered with marketFactory. A malicious contract could exploit the DSU approval in Account.marketTransfer (unlimited approval without validation) to drain account funds. Requires owner signature (phishing/compromised signer risk).

findings.title: Attack Chain: Nonce Griefing + Rebalance Drain via Phishing
findings.description: Combining VULN-032 signer-account mismatch with VULN-103 arbitrary market addresses and VULN-100 nonce manipulation to create a phishing-assisted fund drain through the rebalance system.

findings.title: Attack Chain: Funding Rate Shock + Accumulator Overflow + Market Freeze
findings.description: Zero-liquidity period causes funding rate accumulation shock. Combined with accumulator overflow potential and coordinator parameter manipulation to freeze market operations through arithmetic panics.

findings.title: Attack Chain: Oracle Price Manipulation Persistent Chain
findings.description: Combining invalid oracle version contamination (VULN-119), Pyth timestamp validation gaps (VULN-082), and keeper commit frontrunning (VULN-080) to create persistent price manipulation affecting settlement across multiple versions.

findings.title: Attack Chain: Pending DoS + Fee Theft + Oracle Freeze
findings.description: Combining pending order slot saturation (VULN-036), settlement fee extraction from invalidated orders (VULN-115), and Oracle.claimFee underflow (VULN-085) to create cascading denial of service with fee theft.

findings.title: Attack Chain: Parameter Trap + Margin Manipulation + Liquidation Cascade
findings.description: Coordinator risk parameter changes on pending orders (VULN-096) combined with zero margin manipulation (VULN-090) and pending slot DoS (VULN-036) to trigger mass liquidations with blocked collateral deposits.

findings.title: Keeper Commit Frontrunning Enables Stale Price Selection
findings.description: Competitive keepers can frontrun oracle commits to select favorable price versions for settlement. While the competitive keeper market provides some mitigation, the lack of commit ordering guarantees creates MEV opportunities for keeper-trader collusion.

findings.title: Pyth Price Timestamp Validation Window Allows Bounded Staleness
findings.description: The validFrom/validTo window for Pyth price validation allows prices within the acceptable window but does not guarantee freshness relative to the actual oracle request timestamp. This creates a bounded but exploitable staleness window.

findings.title: Oracle.claimFee() Underflow Revert Blocks Fee Claims
findings.description: Oracle.claimFee() can revert due to arithmetic underflow if accumulated fees are insufficient, blocking fee withdrawal for the oracle factory. While unlikely to trigger under normal conditions, it could become permanent if fee accounting diverges.

findings.title: Oracle Request Routing During Migration Creates Settlement Stall
findings.description: During oracle provider migration, request routing can stall settlement for up to one granularity period (~68 seconds). While bounded, this creates a window where no settlement occurs and positions cannot be updated.

findings.title: Coordinator Can Set Zero Margin/Maintenance Requirements
findings.description: Coordinators can set margin and maintenance requirements to zero for their markets, effectively removing position safety bounds. This is a trusted role design tradeoff but creates risk if coordinator keys are compromised.

findings.title: Risk Parameter Changes Apply Retroactively to Pending Orders
findings.description: Risk parameter changes by the coordinator take effect immediately and apply to already-pending orders that were placed under different parameters. Users may be liquidated due to parameter changes made after their order was placed.

findings.title: Settlement Fee Charged for Invalidated Orders
findings.description: When oracle versions are invalid, Order.invalidate() and Guarantee.invalidate() zero position changes but preserve the orders count. Settlement fees are charged for orders that had no effect, extracting value from users for no service.

findings.title: Oracle Migration Routing Stall Bounded to One Granularity Period
findings.description: During oracle provider migration, routing can stall settlement for one granularity period. Pending orders queue up during the stall and settle in a burst when it resolves, potentially causing gas issues and price discontinuities.

findings.title: Pause/Unpause Settlement Discontinuity Creates Accumulation Gap
findings.description: When a market transitions from paused to unpaused, settlement accumulates the entire gap in one step rather than gradually, creating a discontinuity in funding and fee accumulation that could benefit informed actors.

findings.title: Intent Solver Has No Protocol-Level Slippage Protection
findings.description: Solvers filling intents have no protocol-enforced slippage protection. While solvers are expected to be sophisticated actors and expiry bounds the timing window, large price movements between signing and execution can result in unfavorable fills.

findings.title: Manager Stale Oracle Trigger Gaming
findings.description: Manager trigger orders can be gamed by exploiting stale oracle prices to trigger orders at unfavorable times. While InvariantLib enforces staleness at execution time, the trigger check uses potentially stale data.

findings.title: MultiInvoker Interface Fee Extraction Within Operator Trust Model
findings.description: MultiInvoker interface fee mechanism allows operators to extract fees up to protocol-configured maximums. While within the operator trust model, users may not realize the extent of fee extraction when granting operator access.

findings.title: Exposure Insolvency When No Makers Present
findings.description: When all makers exit a market, accumulated exposure has no counterparty to absorb it. claimExposure is the intended recovery path but requires trusted admin action, leaving protocol funds at risk during the interim period.

findings.title: Vault Cross-Market Insolvency Propagation
findings.description: Insolvency in one market propagates to affect all vault depositors due to shared collateral design. A loss in one market reduces the vault's total assets, impacting share prices and redemption values across all markets.

findings.title: Vault Frozen When Any Registered Market Is Paused
findings.description: Vault._settleUnderlying() calls market.settle() on every registered market without try/catch. If any market is paused (whenNotPaused modifier), ALL vault operations revert: deposits, redemptions, claims, settlement, and rebalancing are completely blocked.

findings.title: Attack Chain: MEV Oracle Commit Sandwich
findings.description: MEV-aware actors can sandwich oracle commit transactions to extract value by positioning before and after price updates, exploiting the predictable settlement ordering.

findings.title: Attack Chain: Flash Loan + Extension Exploit (Async Settlement Protects)
findings.description: Flash loan combined with VULN-001 extension exploit. Async settlement provides structural protection since positions cannot be opened and closed atomically, but the extension registration itself is still exploitable.

findings.title: Coordinator.claimFee() Passes msg.sender Instead of address(this)
findings.description: Coordinator.claimFee() passes msg.sender as the fee recipient instead of address(this), making risk fee claims non-functional. The coordinator cannot actually collect its earned risk fees from markets.

findings.title: Coordinator Has Unbounded Market Scope
findings.description: A single coordinator address controls all markets it is assigned to with no per-market granularity or scope limitation. Compromising one coordinator key affects all its markets simultaneously.

findings.title: EIP-1271 Smart Contract Wallet Signatures Blocked by 65-Byte Length Check
findings.description: VerifierBase hardcodes a 65-byte signature length check, blocking EIP-1271 smart contract wallet signatures which may have different lengths. All smart contract wallets are unable to use any signed-message functionality in the protocol.

findings.title: verifyCommon Externally Callable as Unrestricted Nonce Burner
findings.description: verifyCommon() is callable externally and burns nonces for any account without authorization checks, allowing anyone to invalidate pending signed messages for arbitrary accounts by consuming their nonces.

findings.title: CrossChainOwnable Pre-Restriction Window Allows Same-Chain Takeover
findings.description: CrossChainOwnable has a window before cross-chain restriction is activated where same-chain calls can take ownership. The fuse mechanism is irreversible once activated.

findings.title: ProtocolParameter minMaintenance Has No Hard Floor Enforcement
findings.description: The protocol's minMaintenance parameter has no hard-coded minimum, allowing the protocol owner to set it to zero and effectively disable maintenance requirements across all markets.

findings.title: Market Initialization With No Parameter Validation Permanently Occupies Oracle Slot
findings.description: Market initialization accepts parameters without validation and permanently occupies an oracle slot. If initialized with invalid parameters, the oracle slot cannot be reclaimed or reassigned.

findings.title: Zero maxPendingGlobal/maxPendingLocal Blocks All Operations Including Recovery
findings.description: Setting maxPendingGlobal or maxPendingLocal to zero blocks all market operations including settlement and recovery mechanisms. There is no safeguard preventing this parameter from being set to zero.

findings.title: Pauser DoS: Combined Owner+Pauser Compromise Permanently Locks All Funds
findings.description: If both the owner and pauser roles are compromised, all markets can be permanently paused with no recovery mechanism. There is no timelock or multi-sig requirement on the pause function.

findings.title: No Granular Emergency Mechanisms: Only All-or-Nothing Pause
findings.description: The protocol only supports full market pause with no intermediate states. There is no settle-only withdrawal mode or partial pause capability, meaning emergency responses freeze all operations including user fund withdrawal.

findings.title: Cross-Chain Governance Delays Block Emergency Actions on L2
findings.description: Cross-chain governance message passing introduces delays that prevent timely emergency actions on L2 deployments. Critical parameter changes or pause operations are delayed by the bridge's messaging latency.

findings.title: Coordinator Instant Risk Parameter Manipulation Enables Mass Liquidation
findings.description: Coordinator can instantly change risk parameters (margin, maintenance, fees) with no timelock or delay. A compromised coordinator can trigger mass liquidations by suddenly increasing maintenance requirements.

findings.title: Factory Owner Has Instant Unilateral Control Over Protocol Bounds
findings.description: The MarketFactory owner can instantly weaken protocol-wide safety bounds (minMaintenance, maxFee, maxRate) without any timelock, multi-sig, or governance delay. All markets are simultaneously affected.

findings.title: Oracle Factory Owner Can Register Malicious Provider and Migrate Any Oracle
findings.description: Oracle factory owner can register an arbitrary oracle provider and force-migrate existing oracles to it. A malicious provider could return manipulated prices, affecting all markets using that oracle.

findings.title: Vault Owner Can Drain Funds via Malicious Market Registration with 100% Weight
findings.description: The vault owner can register a malicious market contract and assign it 100% weight, directing all vault funds to the attacker-controlled market during rebalancing.

findings.title: Factory Settle-Only Mode Traps Funds With No Auto-Expiry
findings.description: When the factory activates settle-only mode, user funds are trapped with no automatic expiry mechanism. Only the factory owner can deactivate it, creating an indefinite lockup risk.

findings.title: Coordinator Can Maximize Fees and Manipulate Funding Direction
findings.description: Coordinator can set risk fees to 100% (draining protocol revenue) and manipulate funding rate direction via makerReceiveOnly toggle and other parameters, without any governance oversight.

findings.title: Oracle Factory Owner Unrestricted Withdraw and Fee Manipulation
findings.description: Oracle factory owner can withdraw accumulated fees without restriction and manipulate fee parameters, creating a trusted-admin extraction risk.

findings.title: Factory Owner Selective Exposure Claim Allows Positive-Only Extraction
findings.description: Factory owner can selectively claim exposure only when it is positive, extracting value from the protocol while leaving negative exposure for market participants to absorb.

findings.title: Vault _withSpread Underflow When tradeFee Exceeds totalAmount
findings.description: In vault Checkpoint._withSpread(), when tradeFee exceeds totalAmount, an arithmetic underflow occurs causing depositors to lose their entire contribution. This can happen with high trade fees or during volatile conditions.

findings.title: Share-to-Asset Conversion Precision Loss Near Zero Shares
findings.description: Vault's convertToShares and convertToAssets functions lose precision when total shares approach zero. The insolvency fallback returns 0, potentially allowing value extraction through share manipulation.

findings.title: Vault Checkpoint Settlement Ordering Manipulation via MEV
findings.description: MEV-aware actors can manipulate vault checkpoint settlement ordering through oracle price foreknowledge, extracting value from vault depositors by timing settlements to favorable price points.

findings.title: Negative tradeFee (Maker Rebate) Inflates Share/Asset Conversions Above 1.0
findings.description: When tradeFee is negative (maker rebate), Checkpoint share/asset conversion ratios can exceed 1.0, creating an inflation vector where share values are artificially elevated.

findings.title: Vault Checkpoint Assets Understated When Deposits Not Fully Deployed
findings.description: Vault checkpoint underestimates total assets when deposits have not been fully deployed to underlying markets, causing share price to be lower than actual value and disadvantaging depositors.

findings.title: Socialization Burns Recorded Assets During Insolvency
findings.description: During market insolvency, PnL socialization permanently burns recorded assets. Early claimants who settled before the socialization event lose permanently, with no recovery mechanism.

findings.title: Redemption During Insolvency Creates First-Redeemer Advantage
findings.description: During insolvency, users who redeem first get a larger share of remaining assets. Late redeemers receive proportionally less, creating a bank-run dynamic that amplifies insolvency.

findings.title: Deposit/Redemption Front-Running via Market Position Manipulation
findings.description: Attackers can front-run vault deposits and redemptions by manipulating positions in underlying markets to affect the share price calculation, extracting value from other vault participants.

findings.title: Vault Settlement Desync From Different Oracle Latencies
findings.description: Vault registered markets may use oracles with different latencies, causing non-atomic cross-market reads and settlement desynchronization. This creates inconsistent state windows exploitable by informed actors.

findings.title: Market Re-Registration After Removal Causes Vault State Corruption
findings.description: If a market is removed from the vault and later re-registered, stale state from the previous registration can corrupt vault accounting, leading to incorrect share valuations.

findings.title: Vault Multi-Market Rebalancing Lacks Reentrancy Protection
findings.description: Vault rebalancing across multiple markets is not protected by reentrancy guards. A malicious market contract could reenter the vault during rebalancing to manipulate state.

findings.title: Deposit/Claim Ordering Assumes _manage Frees Sufficient DSU
findings.description: Vault deposit/claim ordering assumes _manage will free sufficient DSU from markets. If markets don't release enough, subsequent claim operations can revert, creating a DoS condition.

findings.title: Vault Share Price Manipulation via Cross-Market PnL Timing
findings.description: Cross-market PnL timing differences allow manipulation of vault share prices. An attacker can time deposits and redemptions around settlement events to capture favorable share conversion rates.

findings.title: Vault Checkpoint Uses Slowest Market Timestamp Bottlenecking Operations
findings.description: Vault checkpoint resolution is bottlenecked by the slowest market's oracle timestamp. One slow oracle delays all vault operations even when other markets have up-to-date prices.

findings.title: Vault _socialize Binary Cliff at Zero totalCollateral
findings.description: The _socialize function has a binary cliff at zero totalCollateral, creating a discontinuity where small amounts above zero are fully socialized but zero causes a different behavior, potentially exploitable around the boundary.

findings.title: convertToShares Reverts on Negative totalAssets
findings.description: Vault.convertToShares() reverts when totalAssets is negative (insolvency), preventing any new deposits even when they would help restore solvency. This blocks natural recovery during insolvency events.

findings.title: Deposit Accepted During Stale Checkpoint Window Before Insolvency Recognized
findings.description: Deposits can be accepted during a stale checkpoint window before insolvency is recognized in the vault's accounting, causing new depositors to lose value immediately upon next settlement.

findings.title: claimExposure Operates on Stale Exposure Value
findings.description: Market.claimExposure() reads the current exposure value which may be stale if settlement has not occurred recently, allowing the factory owner to claim based on outdated exposure calculations.

findings.title: Oracle Provider Migration Edge Cases: Orphaned Versions and Settlement Gaps
findings.description: Oracle provider migration creates edge cases including orphaned versions that no provider claims, settlement gaps between providers, stale windows during transition, and boundary issues at the migration version.

findings.title: KeeperOracle Stale Price Carry-Over Has No Freshness Bound After Timeout
findings.description: KeeperOracle carries over the last known price after timeout with no freshness bound. If the oracle times out, subsequent operations use an arbitrarily stale price with no degradation or warning.

findings.title: Settlement Callback Async Fee Enables Fee Drain via Spam
findings.description: Settlement callbacks are paid per-callback with async fees. An attacker can spam settlement requests to drain the fee pool through excessive callback payments to keepers.

findings.title: Granularity Transition Creates Oracle Version Alignment Gaps
findings.description: When KeeperFactory changes granularity, existing oracle versions may not align with the new granularity, creating gaps where no valid version exists and settlement cannot proceed.

findings.title: Unrequested Oracle Version Commit Blocked When Next Requested Version Exists
findings.description: KeeperOracle blocks commits for unrequested versions when a next requested version exists, preventing valid price data from being committed and potentially delaying settlement.

findings.title: Oracle.at() Provider Lookup Off-By-One During Migration Returns Wrong Price
findings.description: Oracle.at() has an off-by-one error in provider lookup during migration, potentially returning a price from the wrong provider at the migration boundary version.

findings.title: Empty Data Commit After Timeout Creates Invalid Version at Zero Cost
findings.description: After oracle timeout, empty data can be committed creating an invalid version at zero keeper cost. This invalid version can contaminate latestPrice through the overrideIfZero mechanism.

findings.title: ChainlinkFactory Commitment Cost Derived From Untrusted Report Field
findings.description: ChainlinkFactory derives the commitment cost from an untrusted field in the oracle report, allowing keepers to manipulate their own compensation by submitting crafted report data.

findings.title: Invalid Oracle Version Contaminates latestPrice via overrideIfZero
findings.description: An invalid oracle version can contaminate the global latestPrice through the overrideIfZero mechanism in Global.update(). Combined with unbounded Pyth timestamps, stale prices can persist in the system.

findings.title: PowerHalf Payoff Loses Sign on Negative Prices
findings.description: The PowerHalf payoff function loses the sign when computing the square root of negative prices, returning a positive value instead of preserving the negative sign. This produces incorrect payoff calculations for inverse markets.

findings.title: validFrom/validTo Lack Ordering Validation — Impossible Window Bricks Oracle
findings.description: KeeperOracleParameter does not validate that validFrom < validTo. If set in reverse order, an impossible validation window is created that permanently bricks the oracle for that market.

findings.title: PowerTwo Overflow for Large Prices Exceeding ~$2.41e20
findings.description: The PowerTwo payoff function overflows for prices exceeding approximately $2.41e20 in Fixed18 representation, causing settlement to revert for extreme price scenarios.

findings.title: OracleFactory.update() No Provider Compatibility Check on Migration
findings.description: OracleFactory.update() does not validate compatibility between old and new oracle providers during migration, potentially breaking price continuity or granularity alignment.

findings.title: Pyth/MetaQuants Exponent Overflow When abs(expo) > 58
findings.description: Pyth and MetaQuants price decoding overflows when the absolute value of the price exponent exceeds 58, as the Fixed6/Fixed18 representation cannot accommodate such extreme scaling.

findings.title: Chainlink Feed Staleness/Negative/Zero Price Not Validated in Gas Oracle and Keeper Fee
findings.description: GasOracle and Kept fee calculations use Chainlink feeds without validating for staleness, negative prices, or zero prices. A stale or invalid Chainlink response could cause incorrect keeper fee calculations.

findings.title: Oracle Value Extraction via Keeper Commit Timing Selection
findings.description: Keepers can extract oracle value (OEV) by selectively choosing which oracle version to commit, timing their commits to maximize MEV extraction from pending settlement operations.

findings.title: No Chainlink Sequencer Uptime Feed Check — Stale Prices During Downtime
findings.description: The protocol does not check Chainlink's L2 sequencer uptime feed. During sequencer downtime, stale prices are used for all operations without any degradation or circuit breaker mechanism.

findings.title: Market Initialization With Unpriced Oracle Allows Zero Price First Settlement
findings.description: A market can be initialized when its oracle has not yet provided any price. The first settlement uses a zero price, potentially creating incorrect position valuations and fee calculations.

findings.title: Accumulated Pending Orders After Sequencer Restart Cause Gas Limit DoS
findings.description: After a sequencer restart, accumulated pending orders must all be settled in a single while-loop iteration, potentially exceeding the block gas limit and creating a permanent DoS on the market.

findings.title: MagicValueLib FULLY_CLOSED_POSITION Arithmetic Underflow
findings.description: MagicValueLib's FULLY_CLOSED_POSITION constant computation can underflow under specific arithmetic edge cases, causing unexpected behavior in position closing logic.

findings.title: Proportional Fee and Adiabatic Fee Division-by-Zero When Scale=0
findings.description: AdiabaticMath6 proportional and adiabatic fee calculations produce a division-by-zero panic when the scale parameter is zero. A coordinator can set scale=0 to brick fee calculations in a market.

findings.title: Coordinator staleAfter Manipulation Blocks Operations or Enables Stale Prices
findings.description: Coordinator can manipulate the staleAfter parameter to either block all operations (very short staleness window) or enable use of extremely stale prices (very long window) for their markets.

findings.title: Efficiency Limit and PController k=0 Division-by-Zero Panics
findings.description: Setting PController's k parameter to zero causes division-by-zero panics in funding rate calculations. Similarly, efficiency limit calculations can panic when parameters are at boundary values.

findings.title: RiskFee Can Be Set to 100% Draining All Protocol Revenue to Coordinator
findings.description: The riskFee parameter can be set to 100%, directing all protocol revenue from a market to the coordinator with no upper bound enforcement at the protocol level.

findings.title: makerLimit=0 Bypasses Scale and Efficiency Validation
findings.description: Setting makerLimit to zero bypasses several validation checks including scale and efficiency limits, creating an inconsistent state where a market accepts no makers but still operates.

findings.title: Global pAccumulator Skew int24 Overflow With Large Imbalances
findings.description: The global PID accumulator stores skew as int24, which overflows with large maker-taker imbalances. Overflow causes funding rate to flip direction unpredictably.

findings.title: Coordinator makerReceiveOnly Toggle Manipulates Funding Direction
findings.description: Coordinator can toggle the makerReceiveOnly flag to manipulate funding direction, ensuring makers always receive funding regardless of market conditions, disadvantaging takers.

findings.title: Rebalance With Zero Group Collateral Causes Unintended Market Draining
findings.description: When rebalance group total collateral is zero, the rebalancing logic can produce unintended market draining behavior, withdrawing funds from markets without corresponding deposits.

findings.title: marketTransferWithSignature Does Not Verify Account Exists
findings.description: Controller.marketTransferWithSignature does not verify that the referenced account contract actually exists, potentially allowing transfers to or from non-existent accounts.

findings.title: Keeper Fee Computation Uses Zero Gas and Empty Calldata
findings.description: Controller_Incentivized computes keeper fees using zero gas and empty calldata parameters, making the fee disconnected from actual keeper execution costs. This allows over- or under-compensation.

findings.title: Zero Rebalance Threshold Enables Perpetual Keeper Griefing
findings.description: Setting the rebalance threshold to zero allows any address to trigger rebalancing at any time, enabling perpetual keeper fee extraction through repeated unnecessary rebalance calls.

findings.title: Rebalance Manages Owner's Direct Market Collateral Without Per-Transaction Consent
findings.description: The rebalance mechanism moves collateral between the owner's market positions without requiring per-transaction consent, only a one-time configuration signature. This grants persistent withdrawal authority.

findings.title: Account Grants Unlimited DSU Approval to Every Market Without Validation or Revocation
findings.description: Account.marketTransfer grants unlimited DSU approval to every market address passed to it without validating the address is a registered market, and never revokes approvals. A malicious address receives permanent unlimited DSU access.

findings.title: Controller Rebalance Doesn't Verify Account Has Sufficient DSU for Net Deposits
findings.description: Controller.rebalanceGroup does not verify the account has sufficient DSU balance before initiating net deposit operations across markets, potentially causing partial execution and inconsistent state.
